meta.title: Global Gas & LNG Flow Intelligence Dashboard
meta.week_convention: Weeks run Monday-Sunday; week_ending is always the Sunday, with data captured up to the 09:00 Europe/Nicosia (Cyprus time) cutoff that Sunday morning.
meta.note: Built from free/public sources (IGU World LNG Report 2026, EIA, IEA, Gas Infrastructure Europe/AGSI, operator statements, Reuters/Al Jazeera/Bloomberg/OilPrice/LNG Prime/Natural Gas Intel reporting) plus a seed infrastructure database. No live Kpler/Vortexa/ICIS feed is connected. Country-level `approximate_current_production` figures are an EI Statistical Review-class ANNUAL BASELINE (bcm/year, ~2023-25 vintage) shown for scale only — they are not a confirmed current-week production reading; do not read them as this week's output. Every flow, disruption, and storage figure carries its own confidence tag — see the Data & Method tab.

disruptions.actual_flow_affected: Force majeure declared on China/Italy/Belgium/South Korea contracts, repeatedly extended
disruptions.expected_restart: 3-5 years per QatarEnergy; force majeure on deliveries now extended to early November 2026
disruptions.description: Missile strikes on 18-19 Mar 2026 damaged two of QatarEnergy's 14 liquefaction trains at Ras Laffan (plus at least one associated Pearl GTL train, hitting condensate/LPG/naphtha/sulfur/helium byproducts). QatarEnergy estimates 3-5 years to repair. Force majeure on customer deliveries (e.g. Edison/Italy) has been repeatedly extended and now runs to early November 2026 — 29 LNG shipments affected so far (~3.8 bcm). This is distinct from the Hormuz transit blockage (see separate entry): loading capacity at Ras Laffan is itself reduced by the train damage, on top of — not instead of — the transit chokepoint.
disruptions.source: LNG Industry (20 Mar 2026, 1 Sep 2026); Euronews (31 Aug 2026); LNG Prime (Edison force majeure, 1 Sep 2026); The National (14 Sep 2026)

disruptions.estimated_capacity_affected: ~20 mb/d oil-equivalent normal transit; effectively all Qatari/Emirati LNG exports
disruptions.actual_flow_affected: Qatari LNG exports down ~96% by cargo count (18 vs 509 cargoes H1 2026 vs year earlier); first loaded cargo since July transited 7-12 Sep 2026 (Al Marrouna to Pakistan), but the bulk of the fleet remains idled behind Hormuz
disruptions.status: Critical / ongoing — first test cargo transited
disruptions.description: The 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis (US/Israel strikes on Iran from 28 Feb 2026, Iranian closure/mining threats, naval blockade, further escalation 5-6 Sep 2026) has made Hormuz transit the binding constraint on Qatari and Emirati LNG exports — more severe than the Ras Laffan train damage itself. Ship-to-ship transfers off Oman (outside the strait) are now used to avoid direct transit, each costing $1M+ and 30-35 hours. War-risk insurance has risen from ~0.25% to 3-10% of hull value. The clearest concrete easing signal to date: the LNG carrier Al Marrouna, loaded at Ras Laffan, transited the Strait of Hormuz on 7 Sep 2026 under a Qatar-Pakistan government-to-government arrangement and docked at Pakistan's Port Qasim (Engro LNG terminal) on 12 Sep 2026 — the first Qatari cargo to cross Hormuz and reach a buyer since the crisis escalated in July 2026, carrying 81,936 tonnes of LNG. Several other empty Qatari-linked carriers have also repositioned toward the Gulf. However, Gastech-conference energy executives (incl. Shell's Cedric Cremers, 14 Sep 2026) cautioned that reopening the strait and restoring supply are "two very different things" — physical Ras Laffan train damage, elevated war-risk insurance, and a thin tanker fleet mean exports will stay well below pre-crisis levels for months to years even if transit fully normalises. Iran's restricted-zone declaration and intermittent regional fighting (incl. a drone strike on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline pumping station, 11 Sep 2026) mean this remains a fragile, partial easing — not a resolution. India (~75% Hormuz-dependent LNG), Pakistan (~87%) and Bangladesh (~71%) remain the most exposed importers.
disruptions.source: Euronews (8 Sep 2026); The National (14 Sep 2026, 17 Jul 2026); Bloomberg (7 Sep 2026, 'Qatar Is Bringing Empty LNG Ships Home'); Dawn.com / Geo.tv / Profit Pakistan Today (9-12 Sep 2026, Al Marrouna cargo); Upstream Online (Gastech Bangkok, 14 Sep 2026); CNBC (17 Sep 2026)

disruptions.description: Nord Stream 1's both lines and Nord Stream 2's Line B were destroyed by sabotage in the Baltic Sea in September 2022. Nord Stream 2's Line A survived largely intact and reportedly remains pressurised/filled with gas, but has never been authorised to flow — a US investor was reported in acquisition talks as of March 2026. All four lines across both pipelines remain non-flowing as of September 2026.

disruptions.description: EU gas storage crossed 60% on 13 Aug 2026, the weakest seasonal position since 2009, driven by LNG imports down 4.1% year-on-year and market backwardation discouraging injections. By 13 Sep 2026 the bloc-wide fill had recovered to 68.04% (per GIE AGSI+), an improvement on the August low but still roughly 16 percentage points below the 5-year seasonal average as the Qatar/Hormuz-driven LNG supply crunch persists. Analysts say reaching even 70%+ by November will be difficult.
disruptions.source: Gas Infrastructure Europe (GIE AGSI+, 13 Sep 2026); S&P Global / energynews.pro (17 Aug 2026)

disruptions.estimated_capacity_affected: Slot restrictions to 34 transits/day at 50-ft draft (Sept 2026)
disruptions.actual_flow_affected: LNG-carrier transits structurally lagging even where water levels improve
disruptions.description: Drought conditions returned in early September 2026, reviving daily slot-management restrictions after an easier stretch earlier in the year. Separately, LNG-carrier transits have not rebounded even when water constraints eased, because long-term charter commitments locked many vessels into Cape-of-Good-Hope routing during the 2023-24 drought years.

Poland's segment of the Yamal-Europe pipeline is being formally absorbed into the national gas grid from around 15 September 2026, closing out its Russian-transit role — Poland now sources via Baltic Pipe (Norway) and the Świnoujście LNG terminal instead.

disruptions.actual_flow_affected: Construction/security activity resuming after years-long suspension
disruptions.description: TotalEnergies announced a full restart of all onshore and offshore activity at the long-suspended Afungi LNG project in 2026, describing it as a fresh multi-billion-dollar commitment after the multi-year insurgency-linked force majeure since 2021. Exact restart date and first-LNG timeline not independently confirmed.

change_log.source: Gas Infrastructure Europe (GIE AGSI+, 13 Sep 2026); DiXi Group/Naftogaz (Ukraine)

change_log.summary: Force majeure extended to early Nov 2026; tentative signs of Qatar testing a Hormuz export resumption
change_log.detail: Edison (Italy) confirmed QatarEnergy force majeure now covers 29 shipments (~3.8 bcm) through early November 2026. Separately, Bloomberg reported (7 Sep 2026) several empty Qatari-linked LNG carriers repositioning toward the Gulf, a possible signal of an export-resumption test — but Iran's declaration of a restricted zone and renewed fighting since keep this fragile and unconfirmed as a trend.
change_log.source: LNG Prime / Edison (1 Sep 2026); Bloomberg (7 Sep 2026)

change_log.summary: First loaded Qatari LNG cargo since July transited Hormuz, delivered to Pakistan 12 Sep 2026
change_log.detail: The Al Marrouna (81,936 tonnes, Ras Laffan-loaded) transited the Strait of Hormuz on 7 Sep 2026 under a Qatar-Pakistan G2G deal and docked at Port Qasim on 12 Sep 2026 — the first confirmed cargo delivery through the strait since the crisis escalated in July. Gastech-conference executives (14 Sep 2026) cautioned this does not mean normalisation: reopening transit and restoring supply are separate milestones given Ras Laffan train damage, high war-risk insurance, and a depleted tanker fleet. Added as tender #5 and reflected in the Hormuz disruption and chokepoint infrastructure rows.
change_log.source: Dawn.com; Geo.tv; Profit Pakistan Today (9-12 Sep 2026); Upstream Online (Gastech Bangkok, 14 Sep 2026)
